blocks.text: 111 מוּסָף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 111
uncertainties: The header is cut off at the top of band1. I read its vowels from the full-page image only, at low resolution.

blocks.text: קוֹל שׁוֹפָר כָּפוּף כְּפוּף לֵב אֶחָד. צִיּוּן שׁוֹפָר פָּשׁוּט פְּשׁוּט לֵב אֶחָד. פּוּר יָמִים יוּצָרוּ בָּם לָבוּר אֶחָד. עוֹבְרִים בּוֹ לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי יוֹצֵר אֶחָד.
uncertainties: צִיּוּן: I can't clearly see the dagesh in the yod.
יוּצָרוּ: I can't tell whether the צ has a dagesh. The vowel under it looks like a qamats.
לָבוּר: the dot on the vav could be a shuruk (וּ) or a holam (וֹ). I read it as a shuruk.
פָּשׁוּט at the end of line 1 has a qamats under the פ. פְּשׁוּט at the start of line 2 has a sheva. These are two different words in the print, not a doubled word.

blocks.text: ח׳ סְמוּכִים בְּצִדְקַת אָב הָיָה אֶחָד. נִשְׁעָנִים בַּסְּבַךְ יָחִיד וּמְיוּחָד. מְבַטְּחִים בְּתוֹם וּבְיֹשֶׁר אָב אֶחָד:
uncertainties: The role mark before סמוכים is small. It looks like ח׳ (Chazzan), not ק׳.
בַּסְּבַךְ: the vowel under the ב (patah or hiriq) and the dagesh in the ס are unclear.
נִשְׁעָנִים: the hiriq under the נ is faint.
וּבְיֹשֶׁר: there is a small vertical stroke under the בְ, probably a meteg. I left it out of the text.

blocks.text: ק׳ לְהִזָּכֵר לָמוֹ עֲנִיַּת קוֹל אֶחָד. בְּשִׁבְתּוֹ בַּכִּסֵּא שְׁפוֹט גּוֹי אֶחָד. יַעֲמִיד מֵלִיץ יֹשֶׁר מִנִּי אֶלֶף אֶחָד. טוֹבוֹת לְהַגִּיד בַּשְּׁבִיעִי בְּאֶחָד. חָשׁוּב גֵּר וְאֶזְרָח לַמִּשְׁפָּט אֶחָד. זַךְ וָרָע מֵהַיּוֹם מוּדַע דִּינָם לְאֶחָד. וַאֲשֶׁר מַעֲשָׂיו שְׁקוּלִים עַד עָשׂוֹר יְאֻחָד. הוּא כְּחָפֵץ לְהַצְדִּיק עֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְשׁוּבָה יִחַד. דֶּלֶת פְּתוּחָה לַשָּׁבִים תֵּת צֳרִי לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד. גּוֹלֶה זְכוּת וָרֶשַׁע לְהַגִּישׁ אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד. בְּקוֹר חֶשְׁבּוֹן לִמְצוֹא אֶחָד לְאֶחָד:
uncertainties: בַּכִּסֵּא: the first vowel (patah or sheva) is unclear.

יְאֻחָד: the final letter looks like a ד. The English translation ('there is delay') suggests the intended word is יְאֻחַר, so this may be a misprint or a ד/ר that I misread. The vowel under the ח also looks like a qamats. I transcribed what I see.
יִחַד: the vowel under the ח looks like a patah.
לְהַגִּיד and לְהַגִּישׁ: the vowel under the ל is unclear (sheva or patah).
בְּקוֹר: I can't tell whether the ק has a dagesh.

blocks.text: ח׳ אִם יַשְׁקִיט וּמִי יַרְשִׁיעַ לַהֲשִׁיבֶנּוּ, וְהוּא בְּאֶחָד. אֱמֶת חוֹתָמוֹ לְהוֹדִיעַ כִּי הוּא אֶחָד. לְעֵת תָּמוּט וּכְכַל יַד עַם אֶחָד:
uncertainties: The role mark before אם looks like ח׳.
The mark after לַהֲשִׁיבֶנּוּ looks like a comma in the print. I kept it as a comma.
וּכְכַל: the vowel under the second כ (patah or qamats) is unclear.

blocks.text: קהל וחזן
uncertainties: This is a small rubric in the margin before the large type. The letters are unpointed and partly unclear. It may be abbreviated as קהל וחזן.

blocks.text: עוֹד יִזָּכֵר לָמוֹ מַטַּת שְׁכֶם אֶחָד. זֹאת הַמַּתְמֶדֶת שְׁמַע פֶּה אֶחָד. רוֹגֶשֶׁת נֶשֶׁף וָשַׁחַר לְיַחֵד לְאֶחָד:
uncertainties: This block is in large type. In both occurrences of אֶחָד in the first two lines, the א is a large ornamental glyph that looks a bit like a צ. I read it as א. It is a typographic display letter, not a different letter.
הַמַּתְמֶדֶת: I'm not sure of the 4th–5th letters (ד or ר) or of the vowels. The English 'constantly' supports מתמדת.

blocks.text: ח׳ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא יִפֶן בְּרַחֲמִים וְיָחוֹן עַם הַמְיַחֲדִים שְׁמוֹ עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר בְּכָל־יוֹם תָּמִיד פַּעֲמַיִם בְּאַהֲבָה שְׁמַע אוֹמְרִים:
uncertainties: This is set in smaller type and indented.
יִפֶן: I can't confirm a dagesh in the פ.
עֶרֶב: there is a stroke under the ע that could be a meteg or a printing artifact. I left it out of the text.

blocks.text: קו״ח
uncertainties: This is a small abbreviation before Shema, probably קהל וחזן. The exact form is unclear.

blocks.text: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְיָ אֶחָד:
uncertainties: The divine name is printed as יְיָ.

blocks.text: ק׳ אֶחָד הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ הוּא אָבִינוּ הוּא מַלְכֵּנוּ הוּא מוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ. וְהוּא יַשְׁמִיעֵנוּ בְּרַחֲמָיו שֵׁנִית לְעֵינֵי כָּל־חָי לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים:
uncertainties: כָּל־חָי: the vowel under the ח (qamats or patah) is unclear.
There is no citation printed on the page. The closing words echo Numbers 15:41.

blocks.text: 111 Musaph for the New Year 111

one was chosen; on it they pass to appear before the countenance of the only Creator, relying on the piety of the forefather (Abraham), who was unique in his age, relying too on that sacrifice in the thicket in place of the only son (Isaac), relying on the sincerity and uprightness of the only father (of the tribes of Jacob).
uncertainties: This continues from the previous English page. The line-break hyphens in 'counte-nance' and 'fore-father' have been joined.

blocks.text: להזכר

May they be remembered favourably on account of their unanimous consent (before the Revelation on Sinai) when He sits on the throne in order to judge the unique people; may He set up an upright defender, one among thousands, on the first of the seventh month, the good deeds to proclaim. Stranger and native are reckoned equal in judgment; for the pure and the wicked is judgment pronounced this day; as to him whose good and evil deeds are equal, there is delay till the tenth of the month; since the Lord desires that He may justify, He has set aside ten days for this. Then the door is open to hand out balm to every single penitent. He tests merit and wickedness, bringing each single act nearer and weighing each single one in order to decide on its requital. If He is patient, who could contradict Him and condemn? He is unique, truth is His seal and it proclaims that He is unique, even though the might of the unique people may totter and wave.
uncertainties: The line-break hyphen in 'judg-ment' has been joined. The English runs the Hebrew להזכר and אם sections together as one paragraph.

blocks.text: עוד
He yet remembers their unanimous bowing of the shoulder, when they constantly as with one mouth cry out the Shema, full of devotion at twilight and dawn to declare the unity of the One.
ממקומו
From His dwelling place may He turn in mercy and show compassion to the people that proclaims the unity of His Name. Evening and morning twice each day, do they constantly utter the Shema in love.
שמע
Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.
אחד
One is our God, He is our father. He is our King, He is our helper, He will again let us hear in His mercy before the eyes of all the living: ‘To be God unto you’.
uncertainties: There is a small mark under the 'r' of 'mercy', probably a speck. There is also a small mark below the text block, probably a scan artifact.

notes: Both scans carry printed page 111: s242 is the Hebrew page and s243 is the facing English page.
I transcribed the English page from the full-page image. That image is clearly legible, so I didn't open the s243 bands.

The upper part of s242 (קול שופר … סמוכים) continues a passage from earlier pages. The Kedushah material on this page runs from עוד יזכר through אחד הוא אלהינו. No Kedushah refrain on this page is abbreviated as a cue, so nothing needed expanding.
The role marks ק׳ and ח׳ are small and could be confused with each other. They alternate as I recorded them; please verify them at high resolution.
There are no footnotes or source variants on either page.
The textual issue most worth checking is יְאֻחָד in the להזכר section: the English 'delay' implies יְאֻחַר.
